en.title: Lithuania in Horizon Europe: five years in numbers
en.summary: Lithuania holds 798 participations and EUR 235.9 million in Horizon Europe grants, with a 15.09% application success rate. Figures from the Horizon Dashboard, data refreshed 28 August 2026, extracted 8 October 2026, with top beneficiaries and a Baltic comparison.
en.body:
Lithuanian organisations hold 798 participations in Horizon Europe grants, worth EUR 235.9 million in net EU contribution, and 15.09% of Lithuanian applications are retained for funding. All figures in this post come from the European Commission's Horizon Dashboard. The Dashboard data were last refreshed on 28 August 2026 and were extracted on 8 October 2026.

Key figures for Lithuania

IndicatorValue
Participations (one organisation in N projects counts N times)798, or 0.54% of all Horizon Europe participations
Net EU contributionEUR 235.9 million, or 0.37% of the programme total
Signed grants with a Lithuanian participant598
Unique organisations224
Applications5,189, in 3,735 eligible proposals
Success rate (retained applications divided by eligible applications)15.09%
Grants with a Lithuanian coordinator97
SME participations205, with EUR 65.3 million

Net EU contribution is the amount in signed grant agreements after deducting funding passed to linked third parties. It is not cash already paid. Of the 798 participations, 36 have no signature year recorded in the Dashboard. The coordinator count includes single-beneficiary grants, where the host organisation is recorded as coordinator.

The ten organisations together account for EUR 123.2 million, about 52% of the Lithuanian total. Vilniaus universitetas is the coordinator in 42 of its 93 participations. Higher education institutions receive 37.8% of the Lithuanian total, private companies 24.2%, research organisations 15.2%, public bodies 14.8% and other entities 8.1%. Vilnius county accounts for 531 participations and Kaunas county for 201.

The largest single lines are Widening participation and spreading excellence (EUR 51.3 million), the cluster Food, Bioeconomy, Natural Resources, Agriculture and Environment (32.9), Climate, Energy and Mobility (26.7), Health (25.8), the European Innovation Council (25.2) and Digital, Industry and Space (21.9). Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions bring EUR 15.0 million in 108 participations. Culture, Creativity and Inclusive Society brings EUR 10.0 million and the European Research Council EUR 9.4 million.

The three success rates are close to each other and below the rate for all Horizon Europe applications, 16.79%. Estonia receives about 1.5 times the Lithuanian amount.

Earlier national figures used a different base. In April 2024 the Ministry of Education, Science and Sport (ŠMSM) reported a 20% success rate for Lithuanian participants against an EU average of 21%. That figure is not comparable with the Dashboard rate above.
